courses.title: First Year Experience
courses.description: Designed to assist first-year students in their transition to university life, with a specific focus on success within the Communication discipline, mental and physical well-being, building lasting connections, and instilling a mindset of career readiness. Introduction to campus and industry resources, tools, programs, and personnel that will enrich their college experience and ensure their academic success.

courses.title: Transfer Experience
courses.description: Tailored for transfer students entering the Communication program and aims to facilitate a smooth transition to Cal Poly Pomona’s four-year university environment. Builds on prior college experiences, focusing on understanding university policies and procedures, exploring career opportunities within the communication discipline, furthering academic development and career readiness, fostering community connections, and prioritizing physical and mental well-being.

courses.title: Public Speaking
courses.description: [GE 1C] Study and practice of the principles and skills of effective public speaking, including how to conceptualize, structure, support, and deliver oral messages. Focuses on informative and persuasive speech-making, speech-critiquing, and understanding the role of reasoned discourse in a democratic society.

courses.title: Advocacy and Argument
courses.description: [GE 1C] Study and practice of the principles and skills of effective oral argument, including how to conceptualize, structure, support, and deliver oral arguments. Focuses on how to create reasoned oral arguments, adapt arguments to different audiences, and critique the arguments of others.

courses.title: Writing for Communication Practitioners
courses.description: Editorial, research, feature, and scholarly writing styles, constructions, and structures unique to the communication field.

courses.title: Copyediting
courses.description: Instruction in the editorial process of writing text that is clear, correct, concise, comprehensible, and consistent. Use of the Associated Press style manual and reference materials. Applying appropriate level of copyediting and eliminating bias.

courses.title: Communication Theory
courses.description: Study of contributions of rhetorical theory, linguistics, psychology, and sociology to the development of general communication theory. 4 hours lecture/discussion

courses.title: Media Design
courses.description: Principles and theory of typography, layout, and production of material for media design. Work with Macintosh computers and learn elements of desktop publishing, including word processing, graphic design, and page composition. 3 hours lecture/discussion

courses.title: Video Production
courses.description: Introduces basic video production techniques for mass media applications, including camera operations, video and audio editing, and off and on-camera interviewing. Develops technical skills needed to enhance visual storytelling, emphasizing video editing and production for diverse platforms including social, digital, and broadcast media.

courses.title: Racialized Language, Power, and Identities
courses.description: [GE 6] Cross Listed as: EWS 2238 Explores the role of language and communication in articulating, maintaining, and subverting historically shaped race relations and social processes which produce racial, class, social, and gender inequalities and stratifications. Drawing from Ethnic Studies, Communication Studies, and Applied Linguistics, to provide the tools to develop a theoretical vocabulary for discussing how race, racism, social identities of certain racialized groups, ethnocentrism, eurocentrism, and white supremacy are manifested in dominant language ideologies in the U.S. which in turn invalidate the ways Native Americans, African Americans, Asian Americans, and/or Latina and Latino Americans speak and communicate. Looks at the multiple ways in which our racial, ethnic, age, gender, and class identities intersect, and how they are reflected and reconstituted through communicative practices. Emphasizes the ways in which cultural backgrounds and social identities affect how we interpret the world, and the ways in which socio-historical relationships of inequality in the US shape communicative practices and racialized identities.

courses.title: Intercultural Communication
courses.description: [GE 4C] Considers complexities of communication in a culturally diverse world toward the goal of improving communication effectiveness. Assimilates theory and research from anthropology, sociology, psychology, ethnic and gender studies, conflict & peace studies, and communication. Examines roles of culture, social groups, and individuals in shaping communication.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Communication Research
courses.description: Research methods used to measure the content, process and effects of communications on attitudes, knowledge, and behavior. Research design, data analysis and evaluation in quantitative and qualitative communication research methodology.
courses.prerequisites: COM 106, COM 1106 , or COM 1107 ; and COM 201 or COM 2201 .

courses.title: Applied Communication Internship
courses.description: An intensive communication internship or other individual/group study of the communications process as specified by each option.

courses.title: Special Topics in Communication
courses.description: Contemporary concepts, issues, and skills not regularly covered in the curriculum.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Online and Social Media
courses.description: Online storytelling with an emphasis on social media strategy and engagement. Social media optimization across various platforms.

courses.title: Interpersonal Communication
courses.description: Examination of the variables determining communication behavior. Development of understanding through involvement in a variety of structured face-to-face interactions with other students.

courses.title: Group Communication
courses.description: Variables of communication within problem solving groups; development of conference and discussion skills. Secondary emphasis on group psychology as it relates to problem solving discussions.

courses.title: Organizational Communication
courses.description: [GE 4C] Interdisciplinary theoretical approaches to the study of communication in and between organizations. Emphasis on organizational communication theories relating to managerial, psychological, sociological, systemic, cultural and political views of communication in and between organizations.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Advanced Organization Communication
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 3 units
courses.description: Analysis of breakdowns in communications systems; identification of barriers and constraints to effective message transmission. Emphasis on practical and creative problem solving. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: COM 3314 , and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Advanced Interpersonal Communication
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 3 units
courses.description: Concentrated focus on prominent theories, research, and methods relating to the study of intimate interpersonal communication between friends, partners, and family members. Explores the processes and stages of interpersonal relationships, including how they are created, maintained, altered, and dissolved through communication. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: COM 1103 , and junior or senior standing. Pre or Corequisite(s): COM 2201 .

courses.title: Communication Capstone
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 3 units
courses.description: Completion of a capstone project working independently or in groups, with instructor guidance. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: COM 1106 or COM 1107 , COM 2201 , COM 3316 , and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Professional Writing and Speaking
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12 units
courses.description: Development and practice of specific writing and speaking skills applicable to professional-type settings. Emphasis on creating documents and oral presentations that are clear, concise, compelling, and correct. Includes discussion and analysis of both traditional and emerging modes of message delivery.

courses.title: Persuasion
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12 units
courses.description: Persuasion is examined as affected by messages in various communication contexts. The process is studied through differing aspects of source, channel(s), and receiver(s). Emphasis on contributions from behavioral theorists.

courses.title: Nonverbal Communication
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12 units
courses.description: Examination of prominent theories, research, and methods relating to the study of nonverbal communication at work, home, and play. Includes investigation of the cultural similarities and differences in nonverbal communication.

courses.title: Communication Law and Ethics
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12 units
courses.description: Constitutional, statutory, and case law governing freedom of speech and press, libel, privacy, journalist’s confidential sources, subpoena, search warrant, contempt, newsgathering and freedom of information, free press and fair trial, obscenity, and access to the media. Ethical responsibility of journalists and public relations practitioners.

courses.title: Gender and Communication
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12 units
courses.description: Examination of prominent theories, research, and methods relating to the study of gender and communication. Explores the social construction of gender and sexuality through communication, and how they influence communication practices and, correspondingly, how communication practices reflect and reinforce gendered roles and differing view of sexuality.

courses.title: Family Communication
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12 units
courses.description: Examination of prominent theories, research, and methods relating to the study of family communication. Explores specific communication processes in the context of families and how particular issues facing families can influence and be influenced by communication.
courses.prerequisites: COM 103 or COM 1103 , and COM 201 or COM 2201 .

courses.title: Negotiation and Conflict Resolution
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12 units
courses.description: The role of communication in the productive settlement of interpersonal and organizational disputes. Examination of effective communication strategies used in negotiation and bargaining situations.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence, Media, and the Future of Technology
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12 units
courses.description: Examination of prominent theories, research, and methods relating to the study of how technology functions in organizational settings. Includes how organizations implement and use technological tools, as well as why these tools succeed or fail in meeting the organization’s purposes and goals.

courses.title: Communication Training and Consulting
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12 units
courses.description: Study of the principles and processes of effective communication training and development. Includes how to create, implement, and assess communication training and development programs; how to conduct communication audits for business, government, and nonprofit organizations; and how to provide individualized one-on-one training and mentoring within the workplace.

courses.title: Event Planning
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12 units
courses.description: Application of public relations techniques to planning events. Participation in planning, organization, and implementation of selected event.

courses.title: Cal Poly Pomona Undergraduate Sponsored Summer Experience
courses.description: Enrollment in this 0-unit course allows students to receive university services while participating in a Cal Poly Pomona sponsored summer experience.
